title: I Built a Cricket Intelligence Platform Teams Don’t Share Publicly
subtitle: Inside a T20 analysis platform that answers where, when, against what and why.
description: Inside a T20 analysis platform that answers where, when, against what and why.
blocks: I need to tell you something that might annoy you.
Most of what you see online as “cricket analysis”... isn’t analysis.
Averages without context. Strike rates divorced from conditions. Wagon wheels that look pretty but explain nothing.

**They tell you what happened.** 
**They almost never tell you why.** 
**And they definitely don’t tell you when it will happen again.**
But then I started asking different questions. The kind teams ask. The kind that don’t have easy answers on Cricinfo.
These are smart people with massive budgets. But **the tools don’t exist.** At least not publicly. So I decided to build one.
That gap is exactly what DeepCrease is built to solve.
Every batter and bowler can be analysed by:
- **Matchups** (batter vs bowler, along with role vs role)
- a “weakness” in Powerplay may **vanish** in Middle overs
- a safe zone vs spin may become a risk zone vs pace
- context flips the narrative and the data shows it
One thing I didn’t expect while building this:
How often “weaknesses” disappear when you change phase + bowler type.

Cricket is a context game. 
We’ve just been measuring it wrong.
This is where it gets serious.

- **Individual Scoring Zones** 
→ Where *this batter* actually plays the ball

- **Relative Scoring Zones** 
→ Where the batter accesses zones **more or less than an average batter**
This isn’t a wagon wheel for aesthetics.
*“What does this batter do differently from the baseline?”*
3. Phase-wise Control %, Boundary Intent & Risk Profiles
Instead of generic strike rates, the platform shows:
4. Matchups That Actually Change With Context
*Where Abhishek Sharma has scored against Shaheen Afridi — and how that changes by phase*
- you can see **where the matchup flips**

Where exactly a player has been caught while playing his shots in each phase, tells you where to set the field to trap him. 
USA had a fielder in Deep Cover for Abhishek in Powerplay, which was a great move. Over **26%** of his runs in Powerplay are in this region against pace with **3** dismissals
All of this works across **10+ global tournaments**, including:

Same logic. 
Same framework. 
Different contexts.

👉 DeepCrease doesn’t tell you *what happened* 
👉 It tells you *why it happened* 
👉 And *when it’s likely to happen again*
That’s the difference between content and **decision-making**.
Because this kind of analysis usually lives **inside teams**.

Very few teams even do this properly. 
Almost none of it is visible publicly.
I decided to change that- at least for now.
If this feels *too detailed*- you’re probably the right audience.
The scary part isn’t what this does today.
It’s what this kind of analysis unlocks next.
If you’re reading this and you’re:
- a **player** who wants patterns, not vibes
- or a **team / organisation** looking for an edge
Happy to walk through how this can actually be used for prep and decisions.

Cricket deserves better analysis. 
This is my attempt to build it.
